newsitem.title: USA: Clinton welcomes N. Korean apology on submarine.
newsitem.headline: Clinton welcomes N. Korean apology on submarine.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Sunday he welcomed North Korea's apology for submarine incursion into South Korea's waters last September.

"I am pleased that Pyongyang has pledged to prevent the recurrence of such an incident and has expressed its willingness to work with others for durable peace and stability on the peninsula," Clinton said in a statement.
The submarine incident, in which 26 North Korean commandos went ashore, infuriated Seoul, which put relations with the North into deep freeze pending an apology.
North Korea apologised for the first time earlier on Sunday expressing "deep regret" in a statement that was hammered out with U.S. diplomats.
The brief statement carried by the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) and Pyongyang radio promised no repetitions of the incident.

Clinton extended his appreciation to President Kim Young Sam for his personal efforts to resolve the issue and hopes "discussions can now begin tomove forward on the four-party peace talks...offered last April."
Clinton called North Korea's apology a "significant development, which I hope will contribute to the reduction of tensions on the Korean peninsula."
